newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - June 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - June 29.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- TAYLOR TURNS DOWN OFFERS FROM BLAIR

Martin Taylor, chief executive of Barclays Bank, is thought to have turned down two prestigious government posts including the Governor of the Bank of England. Taylor has committed himself to Barclays at a time of fast consolidation in the retail banking industry.
-- ICI TO SELL HQ TO PRU FOR 100M STG

The Prudential has emerged as the frontrunner to buy ICI's respected headquarters near the Houses of Parliament. The deal worth around 100m stg would be one of London's biggest property deals this year. Earlier this year ICI announced a 3bn stg programme of disposals.
-- MARKET POISED FOR BUDGET SLUMP

Market traders are predicting a stockmarket fall of up to 400 points if the Chancellor Gordon Brown cuts or abolishes the tax credit on dividends in his Budget. The move would affect the dividend income of pension funds and other tax-exempt institutions.
-- LARGE TIPPED FOR NATWEST ROLE

Senior insiders at NatWest are keen to offer the job of chairman of NatWest Markets to the chairman of the Securities and Investments Board when he steps down at the end of July. Sir Andrew Large is being touted as the man to restore the City's confidence in NatWest's investment arm after the recent blackhole in its accounts
-- CARPETBAGGERS INCENSE NPI

National Provident Institute has responded angrily to a mail shot by Hargreaves Lansdown, one of the Britain's biggest firms of financial advisers, encouraging its 250,000 clients to buy policies in NPI on the basis that it is the best bet for a life office demutulisation.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- BROWN'S BUDGET WILL SET OUT TO BOOST INVESTMENT

Gordon Brown's budget on Wednesday will concentrate on education,training and investment according to Treasury officials. The budget could see the gradual abolition of advance corporation tax alongside measures to encourage capital spending.
-- HANSON PUTS GROVE CRANE UP FOR SALE

Hanson's group's corporate development director Robert Hanson is proposing the sale of its Grove Worldwide subsidiary, the world's leading hydraulic crane manufacturer. Goldman Sachs could be brought in to conduct an international auction for the business.
-- GRANDMET'S CORBETT GOES TO RAILTRACK

Gerald Corbett, who unexpectedly stepped down as finance director of Grand Metropolitan last week, is to become chief executive of Railtrack. The job will be his first chief executive post in his career.
-- CITY PUSHES NATWEST TO TEAM UP WITH PRU

Large city investors are to propose to the NatWest board a merger with the Prudential Corporation to halt its poor performance in the banking sector and allow it to compete in global investment-banking. NatWest is currently investigating a 90m stg blackhole in NatWest Markets' accounts.
-- BECKETT TO ABOLISH 'STAR' REGULATORS

The Board of Trade's President Margaret Beckett will this week call for commissions to take-over from utility regulators. She will also outline details of the windfall tax on the utilities in a speech at the Institute for Public Policy Research conference.
THE OBSERVER
-- RAISE TAXES TO CURB BOOM, SAYS BANK

The Bank of England has called on the Chancellor Gordon Brown to raise taxes in next Wednesday's Budget to contain consumer spending. Treasury officials are also concerned that the consumer boom could force up interest rates which would put pressure on sterling.
-- NATWEST ROGUE TRADER

Rogue trader Kyriacos Papoui has told solicitor Linklaters & Payne and accountant Coopers & Lybrand there were already losses on the options dealing book when he took over in 1994. He covered these up and his own subsequent losses by using false pricing information.
-- MURDOCH POISED FOR BSKYB SWOOP

Rupert Murdoch is considering a BSkyB share buyback to increase News International's 40 percent stake in the satellite broadcaster. Murdoch would have to make an offer to large shareholders Pathe, Granada and Pearson if he intends a full share buyback.
-- BLOCKED BASS IS READY TO BET ON A NEW BID

Following the block merger with Carlsberg-Tetley, Bass is expected to renew its interest in the William Hill betting shop chain. However, the move would probably also come under the investigation of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission because Bass already owns the bookmaker Coral.
-- LIDDELL ACCUSED OF 'FASCIST BEHAVIOUR'

Legal & General has accused the Economic Secretary to the Treasury of 'fascist behaviour' after the company was named for making little progress in compensating victims in the pension mis-selling scandal. The firm also warned that it could take up to 10 years to sort out the mess.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- BT SET TO SUE OVER WINDFALL LEVY

Senior executives at BT could stage a legal challenge against the Government if its windfall tax liability is greater than 250m stg. The details of the windfall tax will be revealed in this week's budget. BT believed it was privately assured before the general election that any windfall tax would be minimal.
-- CHINESE SEEK 2BN STG BANK STAKE

HSBC Holdings could be forced by the Chinese authorities to reduce its 61 percent stake in its Hong Kong retail banking subsidiary to 49 percent. HSBC has a dominant hold in the retail market through the colony's largest bank, Hongkong Bank, and its stake in Hang Seng.
-- BROWN TARGETS TAX BREAKS

Gordon Brown's Budget on Wednesday could target offshore tax breaks for corporations and individuals in an effort to raise revenues from capital gains tax. The Chancellor is thought to want to close loopholes that allow companies and individuals to make unlimited capital gains offshore without being liable for tax in the UK.
-- CARLSBERG WOOS GUINNESS

Carlsberg is expected to offer Guinness the chance to buy its Carlsberg Tetley business after the Government blocked Bass acquiring a controlling interest in the firm. Carlsberg is keen to adopt a more international strategy and develop joint-venture operations.
-- ARNAULT HEADING FOR GMG BOARD
The chairman of LVMH, Bernard Arnault, may be offer a seat on thenew GMG Brands board to end disagreements which are threatening the planned merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- PENSIONERS LOSE 110M STG IN NORWICH UNION FLOAT

The insurance giant Norwich Union has been accused of short- changing small investors who applied for shares in the stockmarket flotation and small pension fund who because of tax rules had to sell their free shares immediately.
-- ALLIED COOL AS GRANDMET SEEKS FALL BACK DEAL

Grand Metropolitan is rumoured to have suggested a possible merger with Allied Domecq in case its 23bn stg planned merger with Guinness is blocked by French businessman Bernard Arnault. Arnault owns large share stakes in both Guinness and GrandMet.
-- SCANDAL-HIT BANK PLEDGES TO BATTLE ON

Roger trader Kyriacos Papouis has alleged that he was ordered by a senior at NatWest Markets to cover up losses. NatWest Market's boss Derek Wanless has reassured blue chip clients that the troubled investment arm will not close or face major cuts despite the 77m stg losses.
-- BT MAY BREAK CITY DATA GRIP

Electronic financial information providers Reuters and Bloomsberg could face competition from BT's Syntegra division which installs City trading system. The division is currently working on a deal with a small software company Display.IT to distribute financial data on the Internet.
-- LIDDELL LETS RIP AGAIN

Treasury minister Helen Liddell has told representatives of the Independent Financial Advisers Association that she expects prompt action over the pension mis-selling scandal. Legal & General and Sedgwick Group were named last week as part of the Government's 'name and shame' policy.
